Package io.webagent4j.locator.api

Interface ILocator<E>

public interface ILocator<E>
Fluent immutable query that resolves elements only at a terminal operation.

first() accepts multiple compatible candidates and returns the highest ranked one. single() additionally requires the best candidate to be sufficiently unique. all() returns every compatible candidate after filtering, deduplication and deterministic ranking.

  • Method Details

    • named

      ILocator<E> named(String name)
      Constrains the query to an exact, case-insensitive accessible name.

    • within

      default ILocator<E> within(E scope)
      Narrows the query to an explicit element scope when the backend supports it.

      The scope is applied before target matching and must remain re-resolvable against the current DOM. It is a hard constraint, not a scoring bonus, so a missing or detached scope blocks resolution instead of silently selecting the wrong candidate.

      Scope chaining preserves declaration order: calling within(...) more than once, mixing this overload with the structured-scope overload in any combination, narrows each scope inside the one declared immediately before it, in exactly the sequence the calls were made - never regrouped by scope kind. This is a conjunction, not a replacement: an explicit element supplied after another scope must belong to that current scope - a backend that supports this contract proves that relationship before accepting it and fails explicitly, rather than substituting an unrelated element, if it cannot. An explicit element supplied as the very first scope in a chain needs no such proof.

    • within

      default ILocator<E> within(ILocatorScope<E> scope)
      Narrows the query to an explicit structured semantic scope when the backend supports it.

      The scope is applied before target matching and must remain re-resolvable against the current DOM. It is a hard constraint, not a scoring bonus, so a missing or ambiguous scope blocks resolution instead of silently selecting the wrong candidate.

      Scope chaining preserves declaration order: calling within(...) more than once, mixing this overload with the explicit-element overload in any combination, narrows each scope inside the one declared immediately before it, in exactly the sequence the calls were made - never regrouped by scope kind.

    • tryFind

      default Optional<E> tryFind()
      Attempts a single unambiguous resolution without converting a real locator failure into a silent empty result.

      Returns an empty optional only when the underlying failure is a typed ILocatorFailure reporting a safe "not found" outcome, found either directly or wrapped by an unrelated RuntimeException within a bounded cause chain (see LocatorFailureClassifier). An ambiguous candidate set still raises the normal explicit exception so callers can distinguish a missing match from an invalid search. A failure that carries no typed locator failure in its cause chain — for example a backend disconnect or an unexpected runtime exception — is never treated as "not found" and is always rethrown.
